# Coroutines <Badge type="info" text="class" />

<p class="api-meta">Namespace <code>Lustral</code> · Assembly <code>Lustral.Api</code></p>

A mod's coroutines: methods that run across multiple frames on the game's main thread, with identical behavior on Mono and IL2CPP. A coroutine is an iterator method; each `yield return` specifies when it resumes:

- `null` or [`Wait.NextFrame`](/api/wait#nextframe): in the next frame, after `Update`
- [`Wait.Seconds`](/api/wait#seconds), [`Wait.RealSeconds`](/api/wait#realseconds), [`Wait.Frames`](/api/wait#frames), [`Wait.Until`](/api/wait#until), [`Wait.While`](/api/wait#while), [`Wait.FixedUpdate`](/api/wait#fixedupdate), [`Wait.LateUpdate`](/api/wait#lateupdate)
- another iterator: after that iterator has run to completion
- a [`CoroutineHandle`](/api/coroutine-handle): after that coroutine ends; a `Task`: after the task completes
- Unity yield instructions: `WaitForSeconds`, `WaitForFixedUpdate`, `WaitForEndOfFrame` (treated as LateUpdate), `WaitUntil`, `WaitWhile` and other `CustomYieldInstruction` types, and `AsyncOperation`

An exception stops the coroutine and is logged under the mod's ID.

## Methods

### Start(IEnumerator) {#start}

```csharp
public CoroutineHandle Start(IEnumerator routine);
```

Starts a coroutine. When called on the main thread, the coroutine immediately runs until its first `yield`, as with Unity's `StartCoroutine`. When called from another thread, its first step runs on the main thread in the next frame.

### Stop(CoroutineHandle) {#stop}

```csharp
public void Stop(CoroutineHandle coroutine);
```

Stops a coroutine before its next step. Has no effect if the coroutine has already ended.

### StopAll() {#stopall}

```csharp
public void StopAll();
```

Stops all coroutines started by this mod.
